subject: Realtime stream dropouts and heartbeat failures — urgent
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@crestlineanalytics.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ops@crestlineanalytics.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Realtime stream dropouts — multiple missed heartbeats and chunk stalls

Hi Rachel —

Heads up: starting ~08:45 UTC our production customers saw repeated interruptions on the realtime WebSocket feed for our inference-backed product. Symptoms:
- Token stream halts (no further chunks) for 3–30s, then resumes mid-token
- Client sees repeated websocket CLOSE/REOPEN cycles and increased 502/504s from the proxy layer
- Error rate spiked from ~0.3% to ~7% and p99 latency for initial token jumped from 140ms to ~1.3s

We captured client-side traces and a short server log snippet (attached). This is impacting live demos and feed-backed UIs. Can your team advise immediate mitigations and confirm whether this is an infra routing issue or something in the chunked-transfer/heartbeat path?

Attachments: log-snippet-20260621.txt, screenshot-heartbeat-gaps.png

Thanks —
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform Reliability | Crestline Analytics
liam.oconnor@crestlineanalytics.com
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@crestlineanalytics.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 09:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime stream dropouts — multiple missed heartbeats and chunk stalls

Liam —

Thanks for the fast report and the logs — this is high priority. I've looped in Soojin (runtime/serving) and David (infra) to investigate. Initial asks while we triage:
1) Can you share the full connection-id for a failing session and a HAR-like capture if you have it?
2) Any correlation with model variant changes or traffic spikes (we'll pull metrics but your side helps us correlate)
3) Are you on our hosted pool or dedicated capacity? (I think hosted per the account but want to confirm)

Immediate short-term mitigations to consider (we'll spin these up if you approve):
- Route your traffic to the reserved/dedicated pool we have for you (if available) to rule out noisy neighbors
- Enable the 250ms heartbeat suppression workaround (low-risk, server-side) to reduce false timeouts

We will update within 30 minutes with a current hypothesis.

— Rachel
Rachel Kim
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Realtime stream dropouts — urgent escalation / initial findings

Forwarding initial triage notes — see below for summary.

On Mon, 21 Jun 2026 at 09:27 -0700, Rachel Kim wrote:
> Liam —
>
> Thanks for the fast report and the logs — this is high priority...

Triage summary (so far):
- Observed across multiple edge nodes in us-west and us-east; not isolated to a single host
- Server-side logs show repeated "heartbeat_ack_timeout" events correlated with connection refresh (websocket close/reopen)
- We see intermittent stalls in the chunk assembly pipeline: some partial chunks arrive but are not emitted for 2–20s while the kernel waits on the KV-cache flush path
- Metric snapshots: 5m error rate jumped to 6.9%, 1m p95 token latency = 820ms, p99 token latency = 1.3s; throughput (tokens/s) spiked and then had periodic drops

Immediate actions taken:
- Enabled conservative kernel-fallback path on a small subset of serving nodes (low-risk) — this reduced stall frequency in our internal test harness
- Opened SERV-9812 to track a possible race in chunk assembly / heartbeat interaction (link below)

Recommended mitigations for Crestline (short window):
1) Failover their production routing to the dedicated pool (we can do this for them). This bypasses autoscaled shared hosts that appear to exacerbate the issue.
2) Apply heartbeat suppression for 60 minutes while we continue root-cause analysis (this reduces false-positive timeouts at the cost of slower failure detection).
3) If the customer agrees, we'll deploy a hotfix that bypasses the KV-flush path for in-flight small-chunk frames — patch is low-risk and reversible.

We should also prepare an executive note — this will likely require credit review if the SLA is affected. Marissa: can you please prepare a short board/exec brief if this spreads?

Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com
From: Priya Ghosh <priya.ghosh@crestlineanalytics.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@crestlineanalytics.com>, ops@crestlineanalytics.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime stream dropouts — multiple missed heartbeats and chunk stalls

Rachel / team —

Appreciate the quick response and the suggested mitigations. We are on hosted pool for this environment. We authorise the following immediately:
- Failover to dedicated pool for the next 2 hours
- Enable heartbeat suppression for the maintenance window

We expect:
1) A timeline for root-cause and an ETA for a permanent fix (we need a preliminary RCA within 24 hours)
2) A formal note on SLA impact and proposed credit/compensation — this disruption hit three high-touch demos and one customer trial today
3) A confirmed contact for exec-level communication (we will escalate if outages continue)

We'll also attach a HAR from a failing session to the Drive link you provided. Please confirm when the failover is complete.

Thanks —
Priya
Priya Ghosh
Director, Product Ops | Crestline Analytics
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Ghosh <priya.ghosh@crestlineanalytics.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@crestlineanalytics.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 17:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime stream dropouts — multiple missed heartbeats and chunk stalls (summary & next steps)

Priya / Liam —

Quick update and action plan after the 24hr triage window:
- Failover to your dedicated pool completed at 09:55 UTC on 21 Jun. We observed immediate reduction in stall incidents (error rate down to ~0.9% in the dedicated pool).
- Heartbeat suppression enabled at 09:58 UTC; this reduced false-close events and stabilized p99 token latency to ~310ms during the window.
- Deployed a reversible hotfix at 15:30 UTC (bypasses the KV-flush path for small partial-chunks). Early results on canary nodes show elimination of the 2–20s holds in chunk emission. Patch attached: workaround-patch.diff

Owners & next steps:
- Soojin / Serving runtime: complete post-deployment verification across all serving clusters and prepare RCA draft (target: 24h)
- David / Infra: perform deeper network/edge node correlation and validate no proxy-level misconfigurations (target: 48h)
- Rachel / CS: coordinate SLA credit conversation and prepare exec note for the customer and internal leadership (Marissa to draft an exec brief)

Requested from Crestline: the HAR captures you mentioned and any client logs that show the CLOSE/REOPEN sequence with timestamps. We will use those to align trace IDs and confirm that no client-side middlebox is interfering.

I'll schedule a 30-minute sync with product/eng/ops and Crestline for tomorrow to walk through the RCA draft. If this is satisfactory, we'll close SERV-9812 once we have post-fix telemetry for 48 hours.

— Rachel
Rachel Kim
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
